slides.say: There are only two reasons a component renders.

slides.text: 1. The initial render. 2. Its state, or an ancestor’s state, was updated.
slides.say: One: it is the initial render. Two: its own state, or the state of one of its ancestors, was updated.
Rendering means React calling your components. Say Page updates its state.

steps.say: React calls Page, then every component it returns, recursively: List, then Item. App is not re-rendered.

slides.text: By default, a re-render re-renders all children. Rendering ≠ changing the DOM.
slides.say: So by default, children re-render with their parent. But re-rendering is just a calculation. React only changes the DOM where the output differs.
